final_answer:
Across the 1,814 breast-cancer samples that could be cleanly assigned from the sequenced sample’s HR/HER2 status, the four receptor subtypes had clearly different genomic landscapes.

HR+HER2- (n=1,362) was the most luminal/endocrine-like group. Its dominant alterations were PIK3CA (42.5%), TP53 (23.2%), CDH1 (18.1%), GATA3 (18.0%), ESR1 (10.3%), MAP3K1 (9.8%), and AKT1 (6.4%). Relative to the other three subtypes combined, HR+HER2- was significantly enriched for PIK3CA (OR 2.24, q=1.83e-10), GATA3 (OR 3.45, q=5.89e-10), ESR1 (OR 5.64, q=1.00e-08), MAP3K1 (OR 2.77, q=2.71e-04), AKT1 (OR 2.74, q=5.57e-03), and CDH1 (OR 2.27, q=1.63e-05), and strongly depleted for TP53 (OR 0.12, q=3.44e-71). Its copy-number profile was marked by frequent CCND1 (21.6%), FGF19 (19.2%), FGF4 (18.3%), FGF3 (17.8%), FGFR1 (14.0%), and PAK1 (11.7%) amplifications, consistent with a luminal/PI3K/cell-cycle–oriented landscape.

HR+HER2+ (n=132) showed a mixed luminal-HER2 pattern. Its leading mutations were TP53 (47.0%) and PIK3CA (31.8%), with CDH1 and GATA3 both at 12.1%. The defining genomic feature was copy-number amplification of ERBB2 (79.5%) together with frequent CDK12 co-amplification (54.5%); RARA amplification was also notable (25.0%). Compared with the other subtypes, the point-mutation spectrum was less unique than the CNA pattern, but TP53 was still significantly elevated (OR 1.71, q=2.23e-02).

HR-HER2+ (n=70) was also dominated by the HER2 amplicon but was much more TP53-heavy than HR+HER2+. TP53 was mutated in 78.6% and PIK3CA in 32.9%; NF1 reached 11.4%. ERBB2 amplification was present in 90.0% and CDK12 amplification in 60.0%. TP53 was strongly enriched versus non-HR-HER2+ tumors (OR 7.34, q=1.55e-12). This subtype therefore looks like a HER2-driven but more genomically unstable state than HR+HER2+.

TNBC (n=250) had the most distinct and aggressive-looking landscape. TP53 was mutated in 81.2% (OR 11.28 vs non-TNBC, q=3.44e-57), making it the strongest subtype-defining point mutation in the cohort. TNBC also showed enrichment of RB1 mutation (11.2%, OR 7.46, q=2.80e-10) and direct-frequency evidence of additional PI3K/tumor-suppressor pathway lesions, including PTEN (8.8%), PIK3R1 (8.0%), and NF1 (8.0%). In contrast, luminal genes were scarce: ESR1 0.4%, GATA3 3.6%, CDH1 8.0%. TNBC also had the highest mutational burden: median TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS 0.1667 versus 0.10 in both HR+HER2- and HR+HER2+ (global Kruskal-Wallis p=1.82e-09; pairwise q=1.06e-08 and 3.62e-07, respectively). On the CNA side, TNBC lacked the HER2 and 11q13 luminal amplicon program and instead showed relatively more MYC amplification and deeper RB1/PTEN loss.

In summary, the subtype landscapes separate into four broad genomic states: HR+HER2- is luminal/PI3K/endocrine enriched; HR+HER2+ is HER2-amplified with residual luminal features; HR-HER2+ is HER2-amplified but TP53-dominant; and TNBC is TP53-high, TMB-high, and enriched for cell-cycle and PI3K-regulator loss-type alterations. These differences suggest different actionable subcohorts within receptor-defined disease, especially HER2-amplified tumors, PI3K-pathway altered luminal tumors, and TNBCs with RB1/PTEN/PI3K-regulator disruption.
